title: WebAuthn challenge consumption is not atomic and its delete result is unchecked
root_cause: consumeChallenge() performs SELECT then a separate DELETE. Two callers can both pass the SELECT before either DELETE commits. The DELETE result is discarded, so a failed delete silently leaves the challenge valid until its 5-minute expiry.
sink: webauthn_challenges table; session establishment via admin magic link
verification: Reproduction RED: two concurrent consumers both claimed one challenge (expected 1, got 2). GREEN after fix. Siblings green (webauthn-auth-options, webauthn-credentials 17/17). Full suite 1110/1110, typecheck clean, lint clean, format clean.
deployment_impact: Live in production since the 2026-07-29 Cloudflare cutover. No deployment change required to fix; code-only.
notes: Defence-in-depth is incomplete: @simplewebauthn only enforces the signature counter when the stored counter is > 0, and synced platform passkeys (iCloud Keychain, Google Password Manager) commonly report 0, which skips that check. updateCredentialCounter() also writes newCounter unconditionally with no monotonic guard and only logs errors. For counter-0 authenticators the challenge delete is therefore the sole single-use guarantee. Attacker capability required: possession of a valid unexpired assertion, so not trivially exploitable - hence P2 not P1. Fix: single atomic DELETE ... WHERE challenge/type/not-expired RETURNING *, plus a monotonic guard on the counter update.

title: Unverified client-supplied WebAuthn public key is later trusted to mint a session
root_cause: POST /api/auth/biometric writes client-supplied credentialId and publicKey straight into user_metadata with no WebAuthn registration ceremony - no challenge, no attestation, no proof of possession. authenticate/verify then reads biometric_public_key back as legacyPublicKey and passes it to verifyAuthenticationResponse as the trusted credential public key.
sink: session issued via admin magic link for the victim user_id
deployment_impact: Live in production since the 2026-07-29 cutover. Code-only fix.
notes: VERIFIED BY ME against source, not taken from the subagent report. Attacker plants their own public key, holds the matching private key, and the signature verifies. Required capability: an authenticated session on the victim account (XSS, stolen cookie, or borrowed device) - so not P0. Impact is persistence: converts a temporary compromise into a permanent password-independent backdoor that survives a password reset, and per the reported BA-0005 other sessions are not revoked on password change either. Fix: stop trusting user_metadata credential material for authentication; require a real registration ceremony writing to webauthn_credentials, and retire the legacy metadata path or gate it behind proof of possession.

title: WebAuthn RP ID and expected origin fall back to client-controlled Host/Origin headers
root_cause: getRelyingPartyId(host) returns host.split(':')[0] and getExpectedOrigin(requestOrigin) returns requestOrigin when WEBAUTHN_RP_ID / WEBAUTHN_ORIGIN are unset. Both inputs come from request headers.
control: WebAuthn origin and RP ID binding
deployment_impact: Not exploitable in current production: WEBAUTHN_RP_ID and WEBAUTHN_ORIGIN are set as Worker secrets and check-required-env.mjs enforces exact values when DEPLOYMENT_ENV=production, so the fallback branch is unreachable there.
notes: VERIFIED BY ME. Rated P3 rather than P1 precisely because the production env vars are set and enforced - the severity is latent, not active. It remains a fail-open shape: any environment that loses those vars silently derives WebAuthn's two anchoring values from attacker-controlled headers, defeating origin binding entirely. Fix: fail closed when the env vars are absent instead of falling back to headers.
